Note that protein breakdown resultant to exercise is considered an important component of exercise-induced hypertrophy because it helps to support amino acid reallocation as well as prevent the buildup of misfolded and nonfunctional proteins (133). After completion of the workout, muscle protein synthesis is increased 2- to 5-fold along with nutrient delivery, with effects lasting 48 hours or more post-exercise (168). An enhanced translational efficiency likely contributes to the exercise-induced increase in muscle protein synthesis (94, 160).
